findings.area: correctness / evidence integrity (new MEDIUM finding F-21.13-3 and the procedure text derived from it)
findings.summary: F-21.13-3 asserts a root cause that the project's own pinned-source research and task 21.9's recorded evidence refute, and that misattribution has already been written into a canonical procedure instruction.
findings.detail: F-21.13-3 claims: 'The administrator GET of /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration does not return the provider ApiKey fields, so a read-modify-write round-trip ... silently DISABLES both providers', and the recommended_action repeats that 'the administrator GET deliberately omits the secret fields'. Three independent lines of evidence contradict this mechanism. (1) The project's own pinned-source research, docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 9.3 (quoting Jellyfin v12.0 PluginsController.cs and BasePluginOfT.cs), states that 'GET {pluginId}/Configuration (GetPluginConfiguration) returns configPlugin.Configuration when plugin.Instance is IHasPluginConfiguration' with no filtering of any kind, and that POST deserializes the request body to ConfigurationType and calls UpdateConfiguration. There is no secret-masking step. The plugin adds none either: grep for JsonIgnore/XmlIgnore/JsonPropertyName across src/ArrTags/Configuration/ returns nothing, and ArrConnectionConfiguration.ApiKey is a plain auto-property. (2) Task 21.9 recorded the exact operation that F-21.13-3 says is destructive and it worked: docs/implementation/21.9/live-verification.json L4 observed reads "EXTRA LARGE SAVE: 'admin GET .../Configuration | jq .Renderer.Size=\"ExtraLarge\"' -> POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -> HTTP 204", with no key re-injection mentioned anywhere in that report (grep for 're-injected|reinjected|re-supplied|keylens' returns 0 hits), and both badge items then re-rendered to new ActiveImageIdentities. A re-render is impossible unless both providers were still enabled with valid keys. Task 21.9 additionally performed several further GET->POST configuration saves (L3 byte limits, L4 size, L4 position, the L7 changed-metadata save) and its whole matrix worked. (3) F-21.13-3's own evidence is internally inconsistent with its narrative: the post-wipe administrator GET is recorded as {"size":"ExtraLarge","pos":"BottomLeft","lv":"Warning","s":false,"r":false,"keylens":[0,0]}, but BadgeSize.Medium is the default for RendererConfiguration.Size (src/ArrTags/Configuration/RendererConfiguration.cs:94), so a configuration 'replaced ... with defaults' would report Medium, not ExtraLarge. The wipe is in fact fully explained without any secret-omission theory: the verifier itself issued 'POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration -d {}' (L2 command text) to establish the 204-on-save half of the gating check, and under Jellyfin's documented UpdateConfiguration replacement semantics an empty body replaces the whole configuration with a default-constructed instance. The subsequent L4 save was then 'built from the now-defaulted GET', so it faithfully carried the already-cleared empty keys. The finding therefore describes a self-inflicted destructive request as a host/API contract defect, and the correct statement is a replacement-semantics property of POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration (any field omitted from the body reverts to its default), which is verifiable from the pinned source already in the repo. Because the misattribution has been carried into docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md (the F-21.13-3 bullet asserts the GET 'deliberately omits the secret fields' and instructs all future verifiers to re-supply secrets 'from a separate secret store'), it will mislead the task 21.14 security review and the 21.6 release record about the Jellyfin configuration API contract.

findings.recommended_action: Rewrite F-21.13-3 so the mechanism is the documented replacement semantics of POST /Plugins/{guid}/Configuration (a partial or empty body replaces the entire configuration, so every omitted field reverts to its default), drop the claim that the administrator GET omits or filters secret fields, and reclassify the severity to reflect a property of the shipped Jellyfin save contract rather than a secret-handling defect. Update the F-21.13-3 bullet in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md to match: instruct verifiers to send a complete configuration body (re-supplying the provider fields they intend to keep) because the route replaces rather than merges. Verify the corrected claim against docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 9.3 before republishing. If the verifier in fact observed the GET omitting the keys, that observation contradicts the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 source and needs its own evidence before being recorded as fact.

findings.area: evidence integrity (deliverable report is non-terminal and its run window excludes its own evidence)
findings.summary: live-verification.json is left at status IN_PROGRESS with a 3-minute run window that predates the 12:12:28Z evidence recorded inside it.
findings.detail: The top-level record reads status 'IN_PROGRESS', overall_verdict 'VERIFIED', started_utc '2026-09-30T11:54:00Z', finished_utc '2026-09-30T11:57:00Z'. Two problems follow. (a) The report is not in a terminal state: 21.9, the direct precedent this report supersedes, records status 'COMPLETE' alongside overall_verdict 'VERIFIED', and the testing doc plus PLANS.md plus state.json all assert the run finished. A consumer reading `status` sees an unfinished run. (b) The recorded run window cannot contain the run: the L4 observed field records the reconciliation trigger 'POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc30... -> HTTP 204 at 2026-09-30T12:12:28Z', which is 15 minutes after the recorded finished_utc. The 3-minute span is also not credible for what the report itself describes: provisioning a pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 amd64-musl host (a ~119 MB server archive plus Alpine runtime packages), installing the plugin, running the committed mock fixture on two ports, completing the startup wizard, publishing three items, injecting a total provider outage, restarting the host, uninstalling and restarting again. The comparable runs are 21.4 at 11:24:30-12:12:30 (48 minutes, all its evidence timestamps 11:54:00-12:10:18 inside the window) and 21.9 at 15:06:00-15:33:00 (27 minutes, all its evidence 15:17:55-15:27:00 inside the window). The live-verification.json mtime is 12:23:20Z and state.json updated_utc is 12:26:07Z, both consistent with a run ending around 12:2x, not 11:57. This looks like a report finalized before the L7/L8 evidence was appended (the notes claim incremental persistence), and it was never re-finalized. The fix is mechanical, but until it is done the primary evidence artifact for the release gate carries a self-contradicting header, which is exactly the field a downstream release reviewer or tooling would key on.

Neither the state transition nor that exact request is what the report records. So the doc promotes a served-image divergence with the persisted record still asserting Published into an observed OwnershipLost state transition, and it drops MetadataRefreshMode from the request it names. The doc also says the verifier 'abandoned that prefix', whereas host.prefix_note and F-21.13-2 both say the verifier deliberately abandoned it rather than clear the state out of band because doing so would simulate an undocumented operator action - a materially different reason that a future verifier needs in order to judge whether the caution is trustworthy.
